https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c80n.text: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, One soldier and three civilians were killed by a member of the armed forces (file photo of Russian soldier) By Laura Gozzi Published 4 hours ago Four people have been killed by a soldier in Russian-annexed Crimea in an apparently random gun rampage. The Moscow-installed regional governor Mikhail Razvozhayev said the gunman opened fire on his fellow soldiers, killing one and wounding another. He then went on to kill three civilians in the village of Khmelnytske - two men, aged 71 and 59, and a 64-year-old woman. Three other people were also injured. The attacker has been detained and the motive behind the shooting was being investigated, Razvozhayev said. He has not been publicly identified and local officials have not released information about which branch of the Russian armed forces he was serving with. It was unclear whether the death toll was expected to rise. Razvozhayev said doctors were "doing everything possible to save" people injured in the attack. He also urged people to rely solely on official information and not to "spread unverified rumours" about the motives behind the shooting or the attacker's identity. Russia has controlled Ukraine's Crimean peninsula since 2014. The vast majority of the international community reject the annexation, considering it instead as occupation of Ukrainian land. Russia maintains a large military presence there, which Ukraine has targeted with drone and missile strikes. https://www.theguardian.com/environment/.text: Crocodiles are protected under the 1973 Washington Convention, designed to protect endangered plants and animals from international trade. Photograph: Guardia di Finanza. View image in fullscreen Crocodiles are protected under the 1973 Washington Convention, designed to protect endangered plants and animals from international trade. Photograph: Guardia di Finanza. Illegal wildlife trade Crocodile head found in luggage at Italian airport Man, who had arrived in Turin from Miami via Istanbul, under investigation for smuggling and faces fine or prison Angela Giuffrida in Rome Tue 8 Sep 2026 08.05 EDT Last modified on Tue 8 Sep 2026 11.47 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google An Italian man is facing a hefty fine or possible prison term after the dried head of a critically endangered crocodile was found in his luggage at Turin’s Caselle airport. The man had arrived at the airport in the northern Italian city on a flight from Miami via Istanbul, the Turin unit of Italy’s financial police squad said in a statement. The reptile’s head had been wrapped in brown paper packaging in an effort to conceal it from security checks and customs, the statement added. It was swiftly seized by border authorities and the passenger, who was reportedly returning from a holiday, placed under investigation on allegations of smuggling a specimen belonging to a protected species. Crocodiles are protected under the Washington Convention, a global agreement signed in 1973 to protect endangered plants and animals from the risk of international trade. If convicted, the man faces a fine of between €20,000 and €200,000, or a prison term of six months to a year. Police said the operation in Turin was part of a wider crackdown in Italy on the illegal wildlife trade. “The item was seized because it had been imported without the required certificate or licence,” police said. Italy is a major transit hub for the illegal trade of exotic animals, much of it rooted in organised crime. In a report published earlier this year, the Italian branch of the WWF said animals including “tortoises, ornamental birds, tropical reptiles and even small primates are illegally traded via online channels and cross-border exchanges”. In 2025, a chimpanzee held illegally in Sicily was seized, the report said. However, items such as dried crocodile heads are sometimes bought as souvenirs by tourists who are unaware that it is illegal to bring them home. A Canadian man was arrested at Delhi airport last year after a crocodile’s head, bought in Thailand, was found in his luggage. https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/14/kaza.text: Kazakhstan is seeking a partnership between the Port of Antwerp-Bruges and its Caspian ports of Aktau and Kuryk as the country looks to expand trade along the Middle Corridor, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev said.Speaking at the Belgium-Kazakhstan Business Council in Astana, attended by King Philippe and Queen Mathilde of Belgium, Tokayev said Kazakhstan was investing heavily in railways, roads, seaports and terminals along the route.“In this context, Belgium’s rich experience as a major European logistics center is particularly valuable to us. We anticipate a concrete partnership linking the ports of Antwerp-Bruges, with the ports of Aktau and Kuryk. This could open wider markets for our metals, petrochemicals and agricultural products,” he said.King Philippe also expressed Belgium’s support for the Middle Corridor, calling for closer links between the route and European ports, railways and logistics hubs.The Middle Corridor, also known as the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route, connects China with Europe through Kazakhstan, the Caspian Sea and the South Caucasus, providing an alternative to traditional east-west routes.A day earlier, Nurlan Zhakupov, CEO of Samruk-Kazyna, Kazakhstan’s sovereign wealth fund which manages some of the country’s largest transport, energy and industrial companies, told reporters on the sidelines of the official welcoming ceremony for King Philippe and Queen Mathilde at Akorda that talks with the Port of Antwerp-Bruges were underway.He said Kazakhstan was interested in drawing on the Belgian port’s expertise and eventually reaching concrete agreements and logistics contracts.Speaking later to Euronews, Zhakupov said the route's viability would ultimately depend on its economic case.“For the Middle Corridor, it has to make economic sense and deliver an economic benefit. That is why negotiations are ongoing — it is a large and complex process,” he said. “I think concrete results are not far off.”Challenges along the roadThe Port of Antwerp-Bruges was not represented at the business council, but the discussion focused on the practical challenges facing the Middle Corridor.Speaking to Euronews after a session on new trade routes between Europe and Central Asia, Ahlers Logistics CEO Dave van den Bos said that while investment in physical infrastructure was already under way, one of the biggest challenges was coordinating handovers between the numerous companies and authorities involved along the route.As many as 15 different companies or authorities can be involved in a single shipment from Europe to Kazakhstan, van den Bos said.“Digitisation is the most important,” he said. “Even if the capacity is there, if you’re standing at the border with your document and waiting for someone to give a green light or a stamp, that’s still going to delay quite a bit. Infrastructure is easier to fix than the whole digitisation of it.”Van den Bos said transit times from Europe to Kazakhstan had fallen from around 80 days to roughly 40–60 days, although port congestion and weather on the Caspian Sea still cause delays.According to Kazakhstan Temir Zholy, the country’s national railway company, the Middle Corridor transported around 44,000 TEUs in the first eight months of 2026, up 58% from the same period last year.Kazakhstan is seeking to increase overall freight volumes along the route to 10 million tonnes, a target Tokayev previously announced.Investment and critical raw materialsBelgium is among Kazakhstan’s ten largest investors, with more than $15 billion invested in the country over the past two decades, according to Tokayev.The forum's sidelines saw 17 agreements covering logistics, agriculture and food processing, artificial intelligence, energy, healthcare and manufacturing.Tokayev also highlighted critical raw materials, stating Kazakhstan already produced 21 of the 34 raw materials considered critical for European industry and supplies Belgium with titanium and molybdenum products.“By combining our resource potential with Belgian investment, technology and expertise, we can build a strategic partnership in this critically important area,” Tokayev said.Belgium and Kazakhstan deepen tiesKing Philippe and Queen Mathilde's visit is the first state visit by a Belgian monarch to Kazakhstan and the wider Central Asian region. President Tokayev welcomed the royal couple with an official ceremony at the Akorda presidential palace in Astana, followed by talks between the two sides.The visit comes ahead of the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Kazakhstan and Belgium next year.“Your visit gives new impetus to preparations for this important anniversary and opens up opportunities to fill our cooperation with concrete results,” Tokayev said, describing Belgium as a long-standing and reliable partner for Kazakhstan in Europe.“We are convinced that we can take our cooperation to a new level,” King Philippe said. “The delegation accompanying me includes representatives from a wide range of promising, forward-looking sectors.”As part of the state visit, Tokayev and the royal couple visited Kazakhstan’s National Museum, the National Children’s Rehabilitation Centre and the Alem.ai International Centre for Artificial Intelligence in Astana.The programme also included a rectors’ forum and a roundtable on critical minerals. King Philippe and Queen Mathilde are due to continue their visit in Almaty.

https://isp.netscape.com:443/news/world/.text: News Home U.S. World Entertainment Money Politics Sports Science Health Odd News Polish police arrest a man suspected of planning to attack Prime Minister Donald Tusk WARSAW, Poland (AP) — A man suspected of threatening and planning to attack Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk was arrested, the country's interior minister said Sunday. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński gave no details about the identity of the man nor the type of attack planned. Poland has been on high alert following a series of school stabbings this week, as well as fears of a possible Russian hybrid attack to weaken Western support for Ukraine in its war against Moscow’s full-scale invasion. “The man who threatened an attack was detained,” Tusk wrote on X. “Thanks to the police for fast and decisive action.” Poland's police had said earlier on Sunday they received information about a possible plot to attack Tusk and Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz. “We take this matter extremely seriously,” said Jacek Dobrzyński, spokesperson for the minister overseeing Poland's intelligence services. He said authorities considered there was a “high probability” the threats would be carried out. Dobrzyński was speaking after an emergency meeting of security services, police and representatives of the Interior Ministry on Sunday. He said information about the threat first reached the state protection service, which then passed it to the police. He gave no other information about the reported plot, but said the intelligence services were receiving an increasing number of various threats with every month. Government spokesperson Adam Szłapka told Polish media Tusk learned about the threat first thing on Sunday morning. He said that, even if officials do occasionally get threats, this one was “exceptionally concerning.” Three attacks at schools in Mazovia province in central Poland took place within four days this week, leaving one dead and many wounded, including children. In September, Tusk warned about likely intensified hybrid attacks by Russia on NATO’s eastern flank. He said Russia was planning strikes with drones or rockets on European countries supporting Ukraine, among them Poland, with the goal of weakening Western support for Kyiv's fight against the Russian invasion. Moscow has denied any such plans. ___ A previous version of the story corrected the day to Sunday. 10/11/2026 11:18 -0400 © Copyright The Associated Press. All rights reserved. https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-needs.text: BRUSSELS—The European Union should have a plan to respond to serious artificial intelligence incidents, two EU countries said ahead of a key Friday meeting of national leaders focused on AI. In a letter seen by POLITICO, Finland and Estonia say the bloc "can still compete at the frontier" of AI by mobilizing capital and building up compute power, but this should go hand in hand with "governing it responsibly." The two countries, considered among Europe's digital leaders, call for "EU-level arrangements for responding to serious AI incidents." Advertisement Advertisement AI safety and security are on Friday's agenda of the first-ever European Council meeting devoted to the revolutionary new technology. Concerns about whether Europe is prepared to respond to AI-powered threats have been picking up steam since a series of incidents this summer in which AI agents went rogue and hacked into other companies. Recent cyberattacks and revelations of coding vulnerabilities have also raised concerns that security systems must be better equipped for the arrival of artificial intelligence. Hungary pushed for a network of national contact points in case AI model providers lose control of their models, in an October paper seen by POLITICO. The country also pushed for a team of "pre-vetted, security-cleared" independent evaluators who can be ahead of incidents. The letter from Finland and Estonia called for investment in European frontier AI models "as an economic priority and as a foundation for Europe's influence on the future of AI." The countries warn that Europe requires "independent capacity to evaluate the most advanced models and their safety and security risks." Advertisement Advertisement
